title: BUILD-NRT-019-rookie-and-udfa-manual-review-queue
universal_lens: The manual review queue formalizes roster truth as a constrained optimization over multi-source evidence. It defines a reconciliation operator that maps raw, timestamped snapshots to a canonical state space, enforcing strict temporal precedence and conflict resolution rules to ensure structural consistency across the entire player graph.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats roster facts as latent variables inferred from noisy official and open-data sources. The reconciliation plan acts as a Bayesian update mechanism, where official evidence serves as a high-weight prior, dynamically adjusting posterior probabilities for team assignments and statuses while flagging stale or contradictory observations.
gse_mapping: In GSE, roster accuracy dictates valid state transitions within the situational reasoning engine. The manual review queue functions as a boundary condition enforcer, ensuring that only verified, non-stale entity attributes propagate into tactical simulations, thereby preventing invalid game states caused by corrupted personnel data.

primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when source schemas diverge structurally or when timestamp synchronization errors create ambiguous temporal ordering of updates.

primitives.name: Temporal Precedence & Authority Resolver
primitives.verbatim_quote: Official current evidence wins unless stale or contradicted by newer official transaction evidence.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Authority: Ordinal weight (Official > Open > Fallback). Staleness: Time delta in SI seconds exceeding threshold T_max.
primitives.assumptions: Official sources are strictly more reliable than open/fallback sources; transaction logs are append-only and immutable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur during simultaneous conflicting transactions from official sources or when network latency causes severe clock skew.

layer2.mapping: Derives a deterministic state transition function for the GSE entity graph based on time-decayed authority weights.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of official overrides and stale record purges.

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Qualified Status: Boolean flag indicating confidence interval width. Verified Timestamp: SI seconds since epoch.
primitives.assumptions: Internal audit tools can perfectly detect conflicts and staleness before public rendering.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks if the validation pipeline lags behind real-time ingestion, causing unverified facts to leak to public surfaces.

layer2.telemetry: Ratio of qualified vs. confirmed facts exposed on public surfaces.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by modeling the NFL roster as a dynamic directed acyclic graph (DAG) where nodes represent players and edges denote team affiliations. The core problem is resolving conflicting node attributes (team, number, status) arising from asynchronous, multi-source ingestion. We define an evidence reconciliation kernel $K(E_1, E_2)$ that computes the similarity and divergence between official and open-data records. This kernel feeds into a temporal precedence resolver, which applies a strict partial order based on timestamps and source authority weights. If an official record $O_t$ exists at time $t$, it dominates any open record $U_{t'}$ unless $t'$ represents a newer official transaction. The system introduces a 'stale' predicate, effectively pruning edges that exceed a maximum time-to-live without confirmation. Finally, an audit validation boundary projects this internal state onto a public interface, attaching a 'qualified status' flag that mathematically represents the width of the epistemic uncertainty interval. Failure modes emerge when the DAG contains cycles due to erroneous trade logs, or when timestamp skew violates the partial order assumption, necessitating a manual review queue to act as a human-in-the-loop constraint solver.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework traces its lineage to distributed systems consensus algorithms like Vector Clocks and Lamport timestamps, adapted for semi-structured sports data. It borrows heavily from Bayesian belief networks used in intelligence fusion, where multiple sensors with varying reliability rates update a central state estimate. The specific application to roster truth extends these concepts by introducing domain-specific authority hierarchies (official league transactions overriding scraped web data) and explicit staleness decay functions, creating a hybrid deterministic-probabilistic model unique to sports intelligence infrastructure.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model three primary agents: the Official League API (high authority, low frequency), Open Data Scrapers (low authority, high frequency), and the Internal Analyst (arbiter). The Official API acts as a rigid rule-enforcer, assuming perfect recall of transactions. Scrapers behave as noisy probabilistic emitters, prone to parsing errors but offering rapid detection of changes. The Internal Analyst operates as a meta-reasoner, intervening only when the automated reconciliation kernel yields high-entropy states or unresolved conflicts. The system must anticipate the scraper's tendency to hallucinate numbers and the API's latency in updating post-game rosters, dynamically adjusting trust weights to maintain a coherent global state.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises if the GSE situational engine attempts to simulate a play using a player whose roster status is flagged as 'unverified' or 'conflicted' by the GSI layer. To prevent anti-collinearity, the manual review queue must enforce a hard block on propagating any fact with a qualified status below a defined confidence threshold into production simulation environments. Leakage occurs if stale open-data records bypass the temporal precedence rule due to clock skew; thus, a cross-layer monitor continuously validates that all active GSE entities possess a corresponding, non-stale official evidence anchor in the GSI truth store.
